A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, renamed from DebugAgent to HiBug2. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on enumeration speed, error-slice discovery, unseen-slice prediction, and model repair, plus a four-participant user study in Appendix A.6.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results and the appendix user study. The framework's renaming does not change their attribution to this work.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same attribute generation, tag assignment, pruning/intersection enumeration, unseen-slice prediction, and repair procedures. The pseudocode and prompts in Appendices A.7–A.8 are unchanged; HiBug2 is a renamed framework.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet bear classes, COCO/private rehabilitation pose data, KITTI car/pedestrian detection data, and web-collected classification repair images. No task, population, or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Domino and HiBug for attribute examples, naive and tree-structured enumeration in Figure 4, HiBug and random selection for repair, and HiBug in the appendix case comparisons and user study.

E3.justification: The model variants, data splits, repair budgets, evaluation metrics, and four-participant user-study protocol remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices A.3, A.5, and A.6. The thresholds M = 10 and C = 0.2 are also retained.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same runtime scaling ablations in Figure 5, cross-model slice-overlap analysis, single-slice repair experiment in Appendix A.1.7, and case studies in Figures 8–12. No additional robustness or diagnostic analysis appears.

E5.justification: Table 2 states averaging over five runs in both versions. Neither version adds seed information, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative examples match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains the proposed method's classification accuracy 0.839, pose AP 0.839, and detection mAP 0.683; the timing results and unanimous user-study preferences are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The slice definition in Equation 1, combinatorial bounds, complexity expressions, and monotonicity reasoning in Section 4.1 are retained. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning structured attributes, efficient enumeration, unseen error slices, and model repair. The claimed 510-fold speedup and approximately 500 CLIP error slices remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning shared failure patterns, tagging errors, generalization, and overlapping slices remain unchanged. Section 4.2 shortens its description of model-independent prediction, consistent with the same prompts already supplied in v1.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the code repository address from cure-lab/DebugAgent to cure-lab/HiBug2 and explicitly identifies it as available code. Implementation details, experimental setup, timing information, pseudocode, and prompts otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work discussion are unchanged. Despite the new HiBug2 name, the paper retains the same comparisons with HiBug and the same positioning within tag-then-slice research.

P1.justification: v3 renames the framework and title, makes limited wording edits in the method, experiments, discussion, and conclusion, and adds Section 8 acknowledging funding. The scientific narrative and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn and moved from page 2 to page 3. Other figures receive limited sizing or spacing adjustments, and labels and captions reflect the new name. The same twelve figures and six tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 mainly updates the framework name, code address, wording, graphics, and funding acknowledgment. These limited presentation and attribution edits preserve the same methods, experimental evidence, uncertainty reporting, and limitations, without establishing a meaningful net improvement or deterioration in paper quality.
